scenario: Technology journalists cover only satellite startups that have successfully deployed at least one orbital asset. Among covered startups the mean funding raised is $85M (σ=$18M). The survival/coverage threshold is $55M raised. The true mean funding across all satellite startups is sought.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

question: (a) Assuming funding raised is normally distributed with σ=18 million USD, solve for the pre-filter true mean μ such that E[X|X>55]=85. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much does the observed (survivor) mean overstate the pre-filter true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: The satellite startups in media after orbital deployment funding raised set is a truncated-normal sample above the 55 threshold. Solving E[X|X>55]=μ+σφ((55−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((55−μ)/σ)=85 gives μ≈82.64556. Only 93.8% of all original units survived; the survivor mean overstates the true mean by 2.3544 million USD.

naive_answer: The true mean funding raised is 85 million USD because that is the observed average among satellite startups in media after orbital deployment.
naive_trap: Survival/publication filters truncate the distribution from below; the observed mean among survivors is a conditional expectation and systematically overstates the pre-filter population mean.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter is equivalent to truncated-normal sampling above threshold=55. (2) Truncated mean equation: μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=85. (3) Numerically solve with brentq → μ≈82.64556. (4) Fraction surviving: Φ̄((55−82.64556)/σ)≈0.93771.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 85,18,55
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-82.64556)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.93771)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
